title: EU Anti-Dumping Case on Chinese Robotic Mowers
seoTitle: EU Anti-Dumping Duties on Chinese Robotic Mowers
dek: Europe's anti-dumping investigation into robotic lawn mowers from China: what is covered, where the case stands, the duty rates reported at disclosure, and what it means for brands, factories and dealers before the 2027 season.
description: WCB's running file on EU anti-dumping case AD745 against Chinese robotic lawn mowers: timeline, scope, reported duty rates, the January 2027 deadline and analysis for Husqvarna, Positec, Mammotion and other brands.

coverCredit.text: Berlaymont building, European Commission headquarters, Brussels. Photo: Euro Pictures, CC BY 2.0

status.label: Disclosure stage · decision due by 19 January 2027
status.text: The European Commission sent its disclosure of essential facts to interested parties on 21 October 2026. Definitive duties, if any, must be decided by 19 January 2027. No measure has been published yet.

summary: On 19 November 2025 the European Commission opened anti-dumping case AD745 into robotic lawn mowers originating in China, after a complaint lodged by Husqvarna Manufacturing CZ. The product scope covers electric robotic mowers that cut grass without direct human control, with or without charging stations and navigation equipment, and both boundary-wire and wire-free models.

The case has moved slowly but steadily. Imports have been subject to registration since January 2026, which keeps open the possibility of collecting duties retroactively. In June the Commission decided not to impose provisional duties, citing the case's technical complexity. In October it issued its disclosure of essential facts, the last major step before a final decision.

Europe is the most developed robotic mower market and the main battleground for Chinese brands that have grown on wire-free navigation, RTK, vision and all-wheel drive. A definitive duty would raise the cost of China-made mowers just as dealers place orders for the 2027 spring season, and would reward companies that have already moved production elsewhere.

keyFacts.label: Scope
keyFacts.value: Electric robotic lawn mowers from China, wired or wire-free, with or without docks and navigation equipment

keyFacts.label: Registration
keyFacts.value: Imports registered from 24 January 2026, allowing retroactive duties if legal conditions are met

keyFacts.label: Provisional duties
keyFacts.value: None; the Commission continued the investigation in June 2026

callout.title: Reported duty rates at disclosure (unconfirmed)
callout.text: Trade publication Motorist, citing a Commission document dated 21 October 2026, reported proposed rates of 45.6% for Mammotion, 47% for other cooperating producers and 53.3% for Positec and other operators. The disclosure is confidential, the Commission has not published these figures, and final rates can change after parties comment.

timeline.title: Complaint lodged
timeline.text: Husqvarna Manufacturing CZ files a complaint alleging dumping of Chinese robotic mowers and injury to EU producers.

timeline.title: Investigation opened
timeline.text: The Commission publishes the notice of initiation for robotic lawn mowers originating in China.

timeline.title: Imports made subject to registration
timeline.text: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/142 orders customs to register imports, preserving the option of retroactive duties.

timeline.title: No provisional duties
timeline.text: The Commission continues the investigation without provisional measures, citing technical complexity.

timeline.title: Disclosure of essential facts
timeline.text: Interested parties receive the Commission's confidential disclosure and can comment before the final decision.

timeline.title: Deadline for definitive measures
timeline.text: The statutory deadline for the Commission to decide on definitive anti-dumping duties.

questions.q: Are EU anti-dumping duties already being charged on Chinese robotic mowers?
questions.a: Not yet. No provisional duty was imposed, and as of early November 2026 no definitive measure had been published. Imports have, however, been registered since January 2026, so duties could in principle be applied retroactively to registered imports if the final decision and legal conditions allow it.

Electric robotic lawn mowers originating in China that cut grass without direct human control, whether they use boundary wires or wire-free navigation, and whether they are sold alone or with charging stations and navigation equipment.

questions.q: How high could the duties be?
questions.a: The Commission has not published rates. A trade publication reported proposed rates between 45.6% and 53.3% from the October disclosure. Those figures are unconfirmed and can change before the final regulation.

questions.q: Does production outside China avoid the duties?
questions.a: Anti-dumping duties apply by country of origin, so mowers genuinely produced outside China are not covered. Simply routing Chinese products through another country can be treated as circumvention, and the EU can extend duties to such flows.

questions.q: How does this connect to the US FCC restrictions?
questions.a: They are separate measures. The EU case concerns pricing and origin, and only covers China. The US FCC Covered List concerns national security and covers robotic mowers produced anywhere outside the US. Together they squeeze China-made mowers in both of the category's largest markets at once.
